<reason>A identified a genuine conflict that B ultimately accepted: valid consent does not legitimate discriminatory medical arrangements. B’s distinction between governing offers and controlling bodies was meaningful, but A showed that prohibiting a willingly chosen arrangement still restricts personal medical choice. B’s forced-treatment examples established autonomy’s importance, not its superiority over A’s equal-standing account of dignity, which also opposed those interventions. A therefore supplied the stronger comparative argument.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s second rebuttal capitalized on B’s concession that consent could remain valid while the scheme should be prohibited. A then directly answered the entitlement defense: lacking a right to demand a particular deal does not make the autonomy interest in choosing it morally weightless.</best_rebuttal>
